query: Earlier studies established BCC refractory high-entropy alloys such as MoNbTaW and MoNbTaVW with excellent high-temperature mechanical properties, while systems including AlNbTiV, NbHfTiV, and AlCrNbTiV also showed favorable mechanical behavior. NbZrTi-based alloys provide broad scope for regulating composition and properties, but changes in elemental identity and proportion can alter both phase constitution and mechanical performance. Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered BCC solid solution with a room-temperature compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa; however, its high Mo content increases the electronegativity difference and is associated with reduced plasticity. Given the constraint of preserving high strength while improving plasticity under room-temperature compression, what single intervention could overcome this limitation? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and its mechanism, predicts quantitative or directional changes relative to equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo, defines the conditions and limits of the effect, cites supporting evidence from the prior results summarized above, and proposes an experiment with explicit observations that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Partial compositional substitution of Mo with V in equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo (resulting in a nominal NbZrTiHfMo0.5V0.5 alloy) will reduce the electronegativity disparity that leads to brittleness, thereby enhancing room-temperature plasticity without a significant loss in high compressive yield strength.
generation.material_initial_state: An equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo alloy forming a disordered BCC solid solution with high Mo content and a room‐temperature compressive yield strength of approximately 1719 MPa but limited plasticity.
generation.intervention: Prepare a new alloy composition by partially substituting Mo with V (e.g., NbZrTiHfMo0.5V0.5) via arc melting to obtain a homogeneous disordered BCC solid solution.
generation.conditions: The alloy should be processed under conditions that ensure full mixing and chemical homogeneity (e.g., via arc melting and proper homogenization heat treatment) so that the disordered BCC structure is retained.
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous disordered BCC matrix with a reduced overall electronegativity difference, which minimizes the local bond stiffening linked to high Mo content.
generation.mechanism: Reducing the Mo fraction by substituting with V lowers the electronegativity difference among constituent elements. This diminishes bond embrittlement and facilitates greater dislocation mobility during deformation, while the remaining refractory elements provide sufficient solid solution strengthening to maintain high yield strength.
generation.predicted_outcome: The modified alloy is expected to retain a compressive yield strength close to 1650–1700 MPa while exhibiting a significant increase in room-temperature plastic strain (aiming for an improvement of at least 50% over the baseline alloy).
generation.baseline: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo with a yield strength of about 1719 MPa and limited compressive ductility.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is anticipated for partial substitution levels around 50% reduction of Mo; beyond this boundary, excessive reduction in Mo content might compromise the solid solution strengthening and phase stability.
generation.uncertainty: While the directional improvement in ductility is supported by the analogy with NbHfTiV alloys, the exact quantitative gains and the retention of high strength depend on maintaining phase stability and homogeneity in the new composition. Sensitivity to processing parameters may also affect the results.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloy samples: one set of the baseline equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo and one set of the modified alloy NbZrTiHfMo0.5V0.5 using arc melting followed by identical homogenization heat treatments. Perform room-temperature uniaxial compression tests to measure yield strength and plastic strain. Complement with microstructural characterization (e.g., XRD and SEM/EBSD) to confirm the retention of the disordered BCC phase.
measurements: Total compressive plastic strain until failure
Phase and microstructural homogeneity (via XRD, SEM, EBSD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the NbZrTiHfMo0.5V0.5 alloy exhibits a compressive yield strength significantly below ~1650 MPa or fails to show at least a 50% improvement in room-temperature plastic strain relative to equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo, or if the processing results in secondary phase formation, the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: There are some researches working on the addition of Al [,], Mo [], Ti [], V [], or Zr [], but few of them focus on the elevated-temperature mechanical performance and the overall effect of the constituent elements. To understand the elemental effect on mechanical properties, equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy is firstly designed as a base alloy by adding the high modulus refractory element Mo to HfNbTaTiZr. Then the subtraction method is used to analyze each elemental effect in the equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr. Thus, in this study, six alloys HfMoNbTaTiZr, HfNbTaTiZr, HfMoTaTiZr, HfMoNbTiZr, HfMoNbTaZr, and HfMoNbTaTi are investigated and compared on their microstructure. Further, the compressive properties at room temperature and at elevated temperature are investigated. By comparing HfMoNbTaTiZr and HfNbTaTiZr, the influence of the addition of Mo can be understood. Likewise, the influence of the addition of Nb, Ta, Ti, or Zr can be articulated. In addition, promising compositions were found and further improved design is suggested. The solid solution phase formation rule and the solid solution strengthening effect will be discussed.

proposals.intervention: Partial compositional substitution of Mo with V (e.g., design NbZrTiHfMo0.5V0.5)
proposals.conditions: Prepare the alloy via arc melting to achieve a homogenous disordered BCC solid solution; test room‐temperature compression properties.
proposals.structural_mediator: Retention of a disordered BCC matrix with reduced electronegativity disparity
proposals.mechanism: Reducing the Mo fraction lowers the overall electronegativity difference, thereby decreasing solid-solution brittleness while maintaining significant solution strengthening. The addition of V, as observed in NbHfTiV alloys, is known to enhance ductility through more facile dislocation motion.
proposals.predicted_outcome: A modest retention of high compressive yield strength (close to ~1650–1700 MPa) while improving room-temperature plastic strain by at least 50% relative to equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: By directly targeting the high Mo content that is linked with increased electronegativity difference and embrittlement, this compositional tweak reduces the embrittling effect without substantially compromising the alloy’s high strength.

proposals.intervention: Thermomechanical processing via severe cold work (e.g., 80% cold rolling) followed by a short-time annealing treatment
proposals.conditions: Cold roll the cast alloy to high strain followed by an annealing at ~900°C for 10 minutes to achieve ultrafine, equiaxed grains while maintaining the disordered BCC phase.
proposals.structural_mediator: A refined grain structure with increased grain-boundary density
proposals.mechanism: Grain refinement strengthens the alloy via Hall–Petch effects and enhances ductility by promoting activation of multiple slip systems. The thermomechanical processing helps disperse any local compositional inhomogeneities (especially any Mo clusters) that could act as crack initiators.
proposals.predicted_outcome: Retention of high yield strength (~1650–1700 MPa) with a significant improvement in plastic strain (potentially doubling room-temperature ductility compared to the as-cast state).
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This processing approach improves plasticity by tailoring the microstructure without altering the baseline composition, thus directly addressing the brittleness associated with high Mo content.

proposals.intervention: Precipitation engineering via a controlled aging treatment to induce nanoscale ductile B2 phase precipitates
proposals.conditions: After solution treatment, subject the alloy to an aging heat treatment at ~600°C for 1 hour to precipitate a fine dispersion of B2-phase particles within the BCC matrix.
proposals.structural_mediator: A dual-phase microstructure consisting of a continuous disordered BCC matrix embeded with nanoscale ductile B2 precipitates
proposals.mechanism: Introducing a secondary, ductile phase can act as local stress absorbers, promoting homogeneous plastic deformation by impeding and deflecting dislocation motion rather than immobilizing it. This mechanism has been shown to improve ductility in alloys with otherwise high strength.
proposals.predicted_outcome: Preservation of the high yield strength (around 1700 MPa) with an increased room-temperature plasticity (an increase in strain by 20–30% compared to the as-cast solution), due to enhanced cooperative deformation.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This single heat-treatment intervention addresses the limited plasticity induced by the high Mo content while retaining overall high strength by engineering the microstructure to provide both hard and ductile regions.

proposals.intervention: Alteration of the processing route to rapid solidification using melt-spinning
proposals.conditions: Employ melt-spinning with cooling rates on the order of 10^6 K/s to turn the melt into ribbons, followed by consolidation (e.g., spark plasma sintering) to form bulk specimens.
proposals.structural_mediator: An ultra-fine, homogeneous disordered BCC microstructure with suppressed elemental segregation
proposals.mechanism: Rapid solidification minimizes elemental segregation and potential local Mo clustering, facilitating a uniform distribution of atoms. This ultrafine microstructure enhances ductility via increased activation of diverse slip systems and improved strain accommodation while preserving solid solution strengthening.
proposals.predicted_outcome: The resulting alloy should maintain a compressive yield strength close to the baseline (~1700 MPa) while exhibiting an improved room-temperature ductility (an increase in compressive strain of 10% or more compared to the as-cast state).
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: By refining the microstructure and reducing inhomogeneities associated with high Mo content, the rapid solidification process is expected to mitigate the brittleness while maintaining high strength, directly countering the plasticity limitation.

decision.rationale: Direction D directly tackles the identified issue – the high Mo content increases the electronegativity difference that is linked to embrittlement. By partially substituting Mo with V (as evidenced by the favorable mechanical performance of NbHfTiV systems), the intervention aims to reduce the bond stiffness contrast while preserving most of the solid solution strengthening. This compositional modification is a single intervention that promises to maintain the high yield strength (near 1650–1700 MPa) while boosting room-temperature plasticity (targeting at least a 50% improvement in strain), directly addressing the stated limitation.
